contextWindow.value: up to 65K tokens after context lengthening (local attention sliding window 4096)

source.quote:
The context lengthening stage increased the number of tokens the model
     can attend to, while maintaining its core capabilities. We accomplished this
     by continuing to train the model on sequences containing up to 65K tokens.

trainingData.value: licensed publisher data, curated public/open-source datasets, Applebot web crawl with robots.txt opt-out; no users’ private personal data or user interactions; filters for PII, profanity, unsafe material; synthetic data used in pre- and post-training

source.quote:
We do not use our users’ private personal data or user interactions when training
our foundation models. Additionally, we take steps to apply filters to remove certain
categories of personally identifiable information and to exclude profanity and unsafe
material.

trainingCompute.value: server pre-training on 8192 v5p Cloud TPU accelerators (4×2048 chip slices) for 13.4T tokens

source.quote:
We trained our server model on 8192 v5p Cloud TPU accelerators provisioned as
4 × 2048 chip slices using the AXLearn [Lee et al., 2025] framework. Training was
conducted with a combination of data parallelism, fully-sharded-data-parallel, and
the newly introduced track parallelism for 13.4T tokens

topics.headline: Built-in safety guardrails mitigate harmful model input and output; targeted safety evals for high-risk content

source.quote:
The framework enforces a base level of safety with built-in safety
guardrails to mitigate harmful model input and output.

topics.headline: Identifies and mitigates susceptibility to prompt injections as an inherent foundation-model risk

source.quote:
we have continued to identify and mitigate the
risks inherent to the use of foundation models, such as hallucinations and susceptibility
to prompt injections.

topics.headline: Hallucinations listed as an inherent risk they continue to identify and mitigate

source.quote:
we have continued to identify and mitigate the
risks inherent to the use of foundation models, such as hallucinations and susceptibility
to prompt injections.

topics.headline: Safety taxonomy includes Algorithmic Biases and Stereotypes; culture-specific bias mitigation datasets

source.quote:
It
currently contains 6 categories and 58 subcategories, which includes areas such as
Slurs and Hate Speech/Symbols, Controversial and Sensitive Topics, and Algorithmic
Biases and Stereotypes.

findings.text: Safety taxonomy has 6 categories and 58 subcategories (e.g. Slurs and Hate Speech/Symbols, Controversial and Sensitive Topics, Algorithmic Biases and Stereotypes); no numeric violation rates are reported.

source.quote:
It
currently contains 6 categories and 58 subcategories, which includes areas such as
Slurs and Hate Speech/Symbols, Controversial and Sensitive Topics, and Algorithmic
Biases and Stereotypes.

findings.text: Human red teaming was run across features to find locale-specific risks; overrides lists can block harmful outputs (e.g. slur prompts in writing tools or Genmoji).

source.quote:
Finally, we conducted human red teaming across features to identify risks
unique to each locale.

findings.text: A novel prompt-selection algorithm for text-only reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is reported to raise Arena Hard by 4%, AlpacaEval win rate vs GPT4-Turbo by 7%, Agent Sandbox by 10%, [GPQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12022) by 7%, and Math500 by 5% versus a prior text-only dataset (deltas, not absolute scores).

source.quote:
This text-only prompt set, which includes multilingual sets, leads to significant gains
in both auto benchmarks (4% in Arena Hard [Li et al., 2024], 7% in win rate of
AlpacaEval [Dubois et al., 2025] versus GPT4-Turbo, 10% in Agent Sandbox [Lu et al.,
2025], 7% in GPQA [Rein et al., 2023], 5% in Math500 [Lightman et al., 2023]) and
human benchmarks (1.3-2.0% increase in overall satisfaction across various locales)

findings.text: Multilingual RLHF is reported to lift over supervised fine-tuning (SFT) at a 16:9 win/loss rate in human evaluations.

source.quote:
In human evaluations we find that RLHF provides significant lift over SFT,
leading to 16:9 win/loss rate.

findings.text: Human graders’ preferences differ on about 20–30% of preference data used for the reward model.

source.quote:
The analysis shows
that human graders’ preferences differ for about 20-30% of the preference data, the
prompts of which are usually subjective, difficult, and/or obscure.

findings.text: On-device model is not designed as a general world-knowledge chatbot; Foundation Models framework targets summarization, extraction, short dialog, and similar tasks.

source.quote:
While we have specialized our on-device model for these tasks,
it is not designed to be a chatbot for general world knowledge.

findings.text: Server pre-training used 8192 v5p Cloud TPU accelerators for 13.4T tokens; on-device dense training was about 14T tokens before mixture of experts (MoE) upcycling and distillation.

source.quote:
We trained our server model on 8192 v5p Cloud TPU accelerators provisioned as
4 × 2048 chip slices using the AXLearn [Lee et al., 2025] framework. Training was
conducted with a combination of data parallelism, fully-sharded-data-parallel, and
the newly introduced track parallelism for 13.4T tokens

notes: Technical report (arXiv 2507.13575), not a system card; alsoDocuments=[apple-afm-2025-blog] (blog not fetched). pageCount=27. Covers apple/afm-on-device-2025 (~3B) and apple/afm-server-2025 (PT-MoE). Responsible AI section is qualitative: taxonomy, guardrails, locale red teaming, prompt-injection/hallucination mitigations—no numeric violation rates. Tables 1–3 extracted fully. Figures 4–5 are raster images (page 18) with printed bar labels; the 99 values were read from the images and checked by a second reader (win+tie+lose≈100%). Their quotes are the figure captions. Skipped figures (no printed eval values): Figure 1 (page 2): modeling overview diagram, architectures, no printed values; Figure 2 (page 3): PT-MoE architecture diagram, no printed values; Figure 3 (page 11): distributed asynchronous RL infrastructure diagram, no printed values. Bits-per-weight in Table 3 omitted (compression setting, not an eval score). RLHF improvement deltas (Arena Hard/AlpacaEval/etc.) and 1.3–2.0% satisfaction range put in findings, not evalResults. InternVL-2.5-4B and Qwen-3-4B-AWQ use rawModelName (not top-level seed ids). No named external tester orgs; no riskDecisions.
